WIC7A-01.kills_note: The named kill for *diminished* ('the loss is not fixed ... nearly vanishes') does not rule it out: a variably diminished quantity is still diminished, and 'nearly vanishes' still leaves it reduced. 'Not a sum of independent contributions but a diminished quantity, one that depends on wind direction' reads cleanly. The only thing against it is that the key answers 'independent' more directly - precision, not a kill. nominal/marginal kills hold.
WIC7A-01.free_elimination: nominal, diminished, marginal are all size/reduction words; collective is the lone aggregation word - the singleton is the key.
WIC7A-01.read_aloud_flag: 'not a sum ... but a collective quantity' - a sum IS a collective quantity on the plain reading; the intended sense (arising from mutual interaction) is a stretch of the word.
WIC7A-01.note: REPAIR: replace *diminished* with a non-size word that the passage kills outright (e.g. *cumulative*, killed by the 'not a sum' clause itself), which also breaks the three-small-words cluster.

WIC7A-02.kills_note: 'not a lapse' kills oversight verbatim; 'asked to find cracks that are already large enough to be found' kills anomaly; 'the interval was chosen so that' kills coincidence. All three real.
WIC7A-02.free_elimination: oversight/anomaly/coincidence all carry 'unplanned/bad' valence; vindication is the lone positive - and the stem's 'looks like a near miss ... is, to the engineer' telegraphs a reversal, so the positive singleton wins without the passage.
WIC7A-02.note: Key is correct and exclusive but the item is guessable: reversal frame + one positive option. Author rates hard; the 'not a lapse' sentence hands over the answer. Repair: replace one negative distractor with a positive-valence wrong word (e.g. *a reprieve* - killed because nothing was postponed; or *a formality* - killed by 'with time to spare'/the inspection being load-bearing).

WIC7A-03.kills_note: The kill for *exaggerated* is 'The cycle rating is not wrong'. But the sentence structure is 'not wrong; it is simply X in a setting it was never meant to describe' - the concession covers the rating in its own domain, X describes it in grid storage. 'The rating is not wrong; it is simply exaggerated in a setting it was never meant to describe' is a coherent claim: a 5000-cycle figure overstates life for a bank that dies after a few hundred. The explanation's 'a figure that is inflated cannot be not-wrong' ignores the setting-relative reading the sentence itself sets up. *arbitrary* kill holds (unfounded = wrong, no setting-relative rescue). *conservative* kill holds.
WIC7A-03.free_elimination: exaggerated/conservative are an over/under antonym pair; mute is the only figurative, off-register word in the set - singleton = key.
WIC7A-03.read_aloud_flag: 'mute in a setting' is an odd collocation; a native writer would say silent or irrelevant. Sits close to the register-singleton tell.
WIC7A-03.note: REPAIR: replace *exaggerated* with an option that has no setting-relative escape, e.g. *obsolete* (the passage gives no time dimension and the rating still holds for phones) or *redundant* (nothing else measures the same thing). Keep *conservative* only if *exaggerated* goes, otherwise the antonym pair remains.

WIC7A-04.kills_note: All three kills are the 'but'-clause, as the author says - and that is legitimate here, since the 'seems X, but [11 km]' frame is the passage. excessive cannot precede a 'but' that escalates; approximate and cumulative make 'seems ..., but' unparseable. cumulative is the on-topic trap (drift IS cumulative) and is dead only because of the connective.
WIC7A-04.free_elimination: 'seems ___, but' + a tiny number = a smallness word; negligible/excessive are the only antonym pair and the frame picks the small one. approximate and cumulative are grammatical non-starters after 'seems'.
WIC7A-04.note: Sound but decided by the blank's own sentence; it is a vocabulary/connective item wearing a passage. Not a repair, a difficulty relabel: easy, not medium. Acceptable as a floor item if the batch needs one.

WIC7A-05.kills_note: The *averaging* kill is an inference ('an average would blur the gap'), not a sentence. Master chronologies are in fact built by averaging many cores, and 'guard against this by averaging many trees from a site: a year missing in one specimen appears in its neighbors, and the gap declares itself' is coherent - the odd specimen shows up as one year off against the average. Nothing in the passage says the specimens are laid side by side rather than combined. *culling* is killed only under the 'discard' sense; 'cull' also means 'select/gather from', and 'culling many trees from a site' reads as sampling. *ranking* is dead.
WIC7A-05.free_elimination: Three data-handling verbs plus ranking; no valence tell. Cold, averaging and overlapping are equally legal.
WIC7A-05.read_aloud_flag: 'overlapping many trees' is unidiomatic - one overlaps ring sequences or cores, not trees. The key is the least natural collocation in the set.
WIC7A-05.note: DROP or re-author. The mechanism the passage describes (cross-matching specimens year by year) does not exclude averaging, and the key's collocation is off. If kept: key -> *collating*, replace averaging with something the colon kills (e.g. *dating*, circular), and change the sentence to 'laying ... side by side' so the kill is textual.

WIC7A-06.kills_note: 'the same record, read differently' kills suppressed and amplified; sentence 1 ('produced when ocean waves press on the seafloor') kills explained - the cause was known from the start. Holds.
WIC7A-06.free_elimination: suppressed/amplified are an antonym pair that cancels; explained is the plain option, rehabilitated the vivid one. With the passage covered two remain and the vivid singleton is the key.
WIC7A-06.read_aloud_flag: 'rehabilitated' implies restoration to a former standing, but the hum was never an instrument before; redeemed/promoted would be truer. Minor.
WIC7A-06.note: The colon sentence alone ('the same record, read differently, had become an instrument') decides it. Author rates hard; medium at most. Structural tell: antonym pair + plain + vivid key.

WIC7A-07.kills_note: *durable*: the kill ('fails if a single defect lands') holds only because 'the fraction of working chips' fixes 'fails' at manufacture; a student reading 'fails' as in-service will find durable live. It is the weakest kill in the batch but the passage does supply the yield reading, so I score it holding. *elegant/versatile*: killed by absence - the trade-off sentence credits the small chip with yield alone. That is the standard WIC 'the passage gives no basis' kill and is acceptable, since 'powerful vs ___' with yield-as-cost as the only stated advantage leaves economical as the only supported attribute.
WIC7A-07.free_elimination: All four are positive chip attributes - no valence tell. Cold, all four legal.
WIC7A-07.note: Keep. Best options-only profile in the batch. Author's worry about *durable* being a relative of a live key: I did not query the bank (no insert here); if it is, swap *durable* for *fast* - killed by the 'powerful vs ___' contrast itself and unrelated to failure.

WIC7A-08.kills_note: uniform killed by 'same absolute temperature ... no stress at one site ... emergency at another'; lenient killed by the same clause (lenient to hot reefs, harsh to cool ones = relative, not lenient); coarse killed by 'how far, and for how many weeks'. Hold.
WIC7A-08.free_elimination: uniform/relative are the only antonym pair; 'deliberately ___:' followed by a two-site contrast is readable without the passage. lenient and coarse are off-axis.
WIC7A-08.note: The colon sentence decides it; 'local summer maximum' in sentence 1 is a second giveaway. Author says medium; easy. Sound item, low yield.

WIC7A-09.kills_note: necessitate: permafrost sentence, holds. detect: 'has spread these genes at a speed' - overuse acted, did not observe; holds, though a student who reads selection as 'revealing' latent resistance will hesitate. disguise: contradicted by spreading = more visible; holds.
WIC7A-09.free_elimination: 'did not create X so much as ___ X' wants a verb that is a corrective near-neighbour of create; unleash and detect are the two that fit the idiom cold; necessitate and disguise do not.
WIC7A-09.note: Keep. Genuinely needs the 'spread ... at a speed' sentence. Third instance of the 'not X so much as Y' / 'not X but Y' corrective frame (see cross-item note).

WIC7A-10.kills_note: All three kills rest on 'dismissed as evidence of careless mixing', as flagged, and all three hold - but they are not needed: 'read as ___ ... turn out to be its chief virtue' is decided by the blank's own sentence. 'read as an economy' is also an unnatural phrase, which makes it a non-option before the passage is opened.
WIC7A-10.free_elimination: 'turn out to be its chief virtue' asks for the antonym of virtue; only defect is one. One option legal cold.
WIC7A-10.read_aloud_flag: 'read as an economy in the Roman method' does not read as English.
WIC7A-10.note: Sound, exclusive, and guessable. Author medium; easy. If repaired, make the blank's sentence stop naming the virtue contrast (e.g. end at '... turn out to do the work'), so the 'dismissed as careless mixing' sentence has to be found.

WIC7A-11.kills_note: consistent and precise killed by 'when they scatter, it cannot' - the spread is disagreement; surprising killed by the perturbation being deliberate. Hold. But the since-clause in the blank's own sentence ('the one thing a decision-maker most needs') already selects valuable.
WIC7A-11.free_elimination: 'not a failure but its most ___ product' plus a 'since ... most needs' clause: valuable is the only option the since-clause supports; consistent/precise are killed cold by 'spread' being in the same sentence.
WIC7A-11.note: Sound but decided in-sentence. Author medium; easy. Fourth instance of the corrective 'not a failure but' frame.

WIC7A-12.kills_note: The kill for *minimal* ('the arrangement of the checks, not their number, does the work') denies that fewness is the MECHANISM; it does not deny that the redundancy IS minimal. The same colon opens 'a few bits stand guard over many', and the previous sentence says 'a small number of check bits'. 'Minimal rather than brute' - small versus triple-everything - is a coherent contrast the passage supports twice. Structured is more precise; minimal is not excluded. incidental ('computed from the whole message') and uniform ('unique pattern') kills hold.
WIC7A-12.free_elimination: '___ rather than brute' admits structured and minimal cold; incidental and uniform do not contrast with brute. Two legal covered.
WIC7A-12.note: REPAIR: replace *minimal* with an option the passage kills textually and that does not restate 'a few bits', e.g. *generous* (killed by 'a small number of check bits') or *optional* (killed by the checks being what does the work).

WIC7A-13.kills_note: Hold, but are not needed: 'as a faint pattern laid over the ordinary image of the sky' in the blank's own sentence selects see; 'retina', 'light has excited it', red/blue light all repeat it. smell is a throwaway; remember and calculate are dead cold against 'pattern ... image of the sky'.
WIC7A-13.free_elimination: The appositive in the stem names an image; see is the only perception verb of an image. One legal cold.
WIC7A-13.note: Author rates hard; this is the easiest item in the batch. Sound, exclusive, near-zero discrimination above the floor. Consider a subtler key set if kept (e.g. the blank on 'feel' vs 'see' with distractors sense/glimpse/perceive would actually test the passage).

WIC7A-14.kills_note: warned/reminded: 'Dams upstream trap that sediment' kills both - and they also die cold, since a delta cannot be told anything and the two are a near-synonym pair that cancels itself, exactly as the author flagged. relieved: 'relieve X of Y' in its ironic deprivation sense ('relieved him of his wallet') means robbed, so a sharp student can defend it; the 'retreats by tens of meters' sentence establishes harm, which makes robbed the precise one. Acceptable as a precision distinction, not a clean kill.
WIC7A-14.free_elimination: warned/reminded cancel; 'of the one supply that had been holding both at bay' in the stem makes it a deprivation verb, leaving robbed vs relieved. Two legal cold, one strongly favoured.
WIC7A-14.note: Author hard; easy-medium. Replace the warned/reminded pair with two live deprivation-shaped verbs (e.g. *spared*, killed by the retreat sentence; *cleared* ... of, killed because the supply was not an obstruction) so the item has more than one live distractor.
